issues.t: Harsh or erratic shifting from a faulty engine computer
issues.sym: Hard or jumpy shifts, flaring between gears, delayed engagement and a check engine light, sometimes ending in a transmission that stops working.
issues.why: The engine control module can malfunction and command the automatic transmission badly, which wears it out. Toyota extended warranty coverage on the module and transmission for these years.
issues.next: Have the computer and transmission diagnosed soon instead of driving on it, and ask a Toyota dealer whether any extended coverage still applies to your vehicle.

issues.t: Excessive oil consumption
issues.sym: The oil level drops noticeably between changes, sometimes with blue smoke at startup or a low oil light.
issues.why: The oil control rings on the 2.4L engine do not scrape enough oil off the cylinder walls, so oil gets burned. Toyota addressed this with warranty enhancement ZE7.
issues.next: Check the oil at every fill-up and keep it topped up. Ask a Toyota dealer about the ZE7 program and have an oil consumption test done.

issues.t: Clunk or knock when turning the steering wheel
issues.sym: A clunking or clicking felt and heard through the steering wheel, most noticeable at low speed or turning on rough roads.
issues.why: The steering intermediate shaft wears and develops play. In some cases the steering rack itself needs attention.
issues.next: Have the steering shaft and rack inspected. Replacing the worn shaft usually cures the noise.

issues.t: Rear suspension arm can rust and separate
issues.sym: Clunking from the rear, the vehicle wandering or pulling, or uneven rear tire wear.
issues.why: Adjusting nuts on the rear suspension arms may have been tightened incorrectly during wheel alignment, letting the threads rust and the arm come loose. Toyota recalled these vehicles more than once and the final fix replaces both rear arms.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and have the rear arms replaced. Do not ignore new rear clunks or wandering.

issues.t: Accelerator can be trapped by the floor mat
issues.sym: The gas pedal sticks down or will not return after pressing it.
issues.why: An unsecured or wrong-size driver floor mat can catch the pedal and hold it open. Toyota recalled these vehicles to modify the pedal and replace the mats.
issues.next: Remove any loose or stacked mats and check the VIN for open recalls. If the pedal ever sticks, shift to neutral and brake firmly.

issues.t: Sticky accelerator pedal
issues.sym: The gas pedal feels stiff, comes back slowly, or stays partly pressed.
issues.why: A friction part inside the pedal assembly can become smooth and then grab when moisture condenses on it. Toyota recalled these years and added a reinforcement bar to the pedal.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and get the pedal fix. If the pedal sticks, shift to neutral and brake firmly.

issues.t: Driver power window switch can overheat
issues.sym: The window switch feels sticky or stops working, or there is a burning smell, smoke or melting near the driver door switch.
issues.why: Grease was applied inconsistently to the master window switch contacts at the factory, which can let the switch overheat. Toyota recalled these vehicles.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. If you smell burning or see smoke from the door switch, stop and have it repaired before using it again.

issues.t: Airbag light from a damaged steering wheel cable
issues.sym: The airbag warning light comes on, and the horn or steering wheel buttons may stop working.
issues.why: A flat cable inside the steering column spiral cable can be damaged as the wheel is turned, which can stop the driver airbag from working. Toyota recalled these years.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and have the spiral cable repaired. Treat an airbag light as a safety problem.

issues.t: Side curtain airbags may deploy unexpectedly
issues.sym: Usually no warning beforehand. The airbag warning light may come on if a sensor has failed.
issues.why: Two roll-over sensors in the curtain airbag system can fail, and if both fail close together the curtain airbags and seat belt pretensioners could fire without a crash. Toyota recalled these years.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and have the sensor assembly replaced.

issues.t: Rear outer seat belts can be cut in a crash
issues.sym: No symptom in daily driving. The problem only shows up in a severe frontal crash.
issues.why: In a frontal collision the rear outboard seat belts can be cut by the metal seat cushion frame. Toyota recalled these vehicles to add protective covers.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and have the protectors installed before carrying rear passengers.

issues.t: White paint peeling
issues.sym: The paint flakes or peels away in patches, often on the roof, hood or tailgate.
issues.why: Factory-applied Super White and Blizzard Pearl paint can lose adhesion. Toyota set up a customer support program with extended paint coverage for these colors.
issues.next: Ask a Toyota dealer whether your vehicle and color are covered under the paint support program and have the peeling documented.

issues.t: Torque converter shudder
issues.sym: A shudder or vibration, like driving over rumble strips, during light acceleration at moderate speeds.
issues.why: The torque converter in the 6-speed automatic can shudder as it locks up. Toyota extended warranty coverage for it under program ZH1.
issues.next: Have a Toyota dealer road test it and check whether the ZH1 coverage applies to your vehicle.

issues.t: 12V battery can shift and short, risking fire
issues.sym: Usually no warning. A burning smell or smoke from under the hood is a sign to stop right away.
issues.why: Some replacement batteries are smaller than the original, and the hold-down clamp may not keep them in place. During hard cornering the battery can move and its positive terminal can touch the clamp, causing a short. Toyota recalled these years.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check the VIN for open recalls and have the battery tray, hold-down and terminal cover replaced. Use the correct battery size when replacing it.

issues.t: Hesitation and lurching at low speed
issues.sym: A delay then a surge when pulling away, or jerky shifting in stop-and-go traffic.
issues.why: Shift behavior on the then-new 8-speed automatic. Toyota issued a service bulletin with updated transmission programming.
issues.next: Ask a Toyota dealer to check for and install the latest transmission software (bulletin T-SB-0107-19).

issues.t: Coolant loss and overheating
issues.sym: Low coolant warning, the coolant level dropping with no obvious leak, or the temperature gauge climbing.
issues.why: Coolant loss is the most reported engine complaint on these years. Toyota also recalled some engines because tiny pores in the engine casting could crack and leak coolant inside or outside the engine.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and have the cooling system pressure-tested. Do not keep driving if the engine starts overheating.

issues.t: Front lower control arm can crack
issues.sym: Clunking from the front, odd steering feel, or the vehicle pulling. In the worst case a front wheel can come loose from the suspension.
issues.why: Some front lower suspension arms were made with a defect that lets them crack and separate. Toyota recalled a small number of vehicles.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and have both front lower arms replaced before driving much further.

issues.t: Fuel tank will not fill completely
issues.sym: The pump clicks off early, the gauge does not show full after filling, and the distance-to-empty reading is shorter than expected.
issues.why: Variation in the fuel tank shape lets the fuel level sender tilt, so the tank fills short and the gauge reads low. Toyota offered coverage for repairs.
issues.next: Ask a Toyota dealer about the refueling support bulletin for these years.

issues.t: Corroded high-voltage cable under the floor
issues.sym: A hybrid system warning on the dash, sometimes with reduced power. Rust is visible on the cable connections under the car.
issues.why: The high-voltage cable running under the floor to the rear motor can corrode early, especially where roads are salted. Toyota extended coverage on these cables for affected Hybrid models.
issues.next: Have a Toyota dealer inspect the high-voltage cable and ask about the extended cable coverage. Do not try to repair high-voltage parts yourself.

issues.t: Theft-deterrent wiring connector can fail (recall 98V-278)
issues.sym: The alarm or immobilizer behaves oddly and the engine may refuse to start.
issues.why: Terminals inside the theft-deterrent harness connector were made out of spec and can lose contact. Toyota recalled harnesses with certain date codes, mostly sold in southeastern states.
issues.next: Have a dealer read the harness date code and replace it if it is in the affected batch. Keep a spare key routine in mind until it is fixed.

issues.t: Driver airbag inflator can rupture (do-not-drive recall 15V-284)
issues.sym: Nothing shows in normal driving. In a crash the inflator can burst and send metal pieces into the cabin.
issues.why: Moisture reaches the propellant inside the inflator over the years and makes it burn far too fast.
issues.next: Do not drive the vehicle until a dealer replaces the inflator. The recall repair is free and parts are available.

issues.t: Brake actuator seal fault can disable the stability system (recall 16V-198)
issues.sym: The ABS, traction control and brake warning lights come on and the brake pedal can feel different than usual.
issues.why: An O-ring inside the brake actuator can be damaged during assembly, so the unit leaks internally and the anti-lock and stability functions stop working properly.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard, press it much harder than normal. If it sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. Have a dealer check the actuator serial number and replace the unit. Expect longer stopping distances on slippery roads until it is done.

issues.t: Spare tire may be under-inflated from the factory (recall 17V-295)
issues.sym: The temporary spare is softer than the label says when you finally need it.
issues.why: Some vehicles left the plant with the spare set to the wrong pressure.
issues.next: Check the spare with a gauge and set it to the pressure on the label; a dealer will do it free under the recall.

issues.t: Water in the steering gearbox can cut power assist (recall 20V-373)
issues.sym: The steering suddenly becomes very heavy, often after driving in rain or through standing water.
issues.why: Water can get past the steering gearbox cover and reach the electric assist motor circuits.
issues.next: Get the VIN checked and have the gearbox replaced before the assist quits in traffic. The recall repair is free.

issues.t: Reverse camera can stop showing a picture (recall 19V-576)
issues.sym: The screen stays blank or shows a blue picture when you shift into reverse.
issues.why: A connector behind the display can be damaged during assembly, so the camera signal never reaches the screen.
issues.next: Have a dealer inspect the connector and replace the display unit if needed; it is free under the recall. Until then rely on mirrors and look behind you.

issues.t: Passenger occupant sensor short can switch off that airbag (recall 23V-865)
issues.sym: The passenger airbag off light may stay on with a grown adult in the seat, or the airbag light comes on.
issues.why: A short circuit in the seat occupant classification sensor makes the system misread who is sitting there.
issues.next: Do not carry an adult passenger in that seat until a dealer replaces the sensor. The recall repair is free.

issues.t: Steering column breakaway pins may be damaged (recall 20V-734)
issues.sym: Nothing is noticeable while driving; in a frontal crash the driver airbag may not protect as designed.
issues.why: Pins that let the steering column collapse in a crash can be damaged during assembly.
issues.next: Have the VIN checked and the steering column replaced; the recall repair is free.

issues.t: Passenger seat can confuse the airbag occupant sensor (recall 22V-519)
issues.sym: The passenger airbag light switches on and off, or shows off when somebody is clearly sitting there.
issues.why: A part of the seat presses against the occupant classification sensor and makes it read the wrong weight.
issues.next: Have a dealer repair the seat and recalibrate the sensor under the recall; it is free.

issues.t: Reverse camera image can freeze or go blank (recall 25V-744)
issues.sym: The backup picture sticks on an old image or does not appear at all when reverse is selected.
issues.why: A software fault in the camera system stops it from refreshing the picture.
issues.next: Have the software updated free under the recall, and in the meantime check behind the vehicle yourself before backing up.

issues.t: Instrument display may hide speed and warning lights at startup (recall 25V-595)
issues.sym: After starting, the cluster may not show the speedometer, brake warning or tire pressure warning.
issues.why: A software fault at startup stops the display from drawing those items.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: you may not see your speed or warning lights, so ease off, keep a safe distance, and pull over where it's safe. Restarting the car once parked may bring the display back; if it doesn't, have it fixed before you drive again. Have the recall done; plug-in models may need the cluster replaced rather than updated.

issues.t: Brake caliper and hub bolts can be loose (recall 24V-911)
issues.sym: A clunk or grinding from a wheel, a vibration under braking, or a wheel that feels loose.
issues.why: Caliper and hub bolts were not tightened to spec during assembly and can work their way out.
issues.next: Stop driving and have a dealer tighten the bolts and replace any damaged parts. The recall repair is free.

issues.t: Front seat bracket welds may be weak (recall 26V-256)
issues.sym: The seat may feel loose or creak; in a crash it may not hold as designed.
issues.why: Brackets in the front seat frame can be poorly welded at the factory.
issues.next: Have a dealer inspect and repair the seat frame under the recall before carrying passengers in that seat.

issues.t: Accessory wheels may have damaged tire valves (recall 23V-485)
issues.sym: A tire on accessory alloy wheels loses air repeatedly or the tire pressure light keeps coming back.
issues.why: Valve stems fitted to some dealer accessory wheels can be damaged during assembly, so they leak slowly, and the load label supplied with them was wrong.
issues.next: Have the valve stems and the load label replaced under the recall and keep an eye on the pressures until then.

issues.t: Rain water collects in the rear footwells
issues.sym: Damp or soaked carpet in the back footwells after rain or a wash, often with a musty smell and windows that fog up easily.
issues.why: Water gets past aged door and tailgate seals and blocked body drains, then runs down inside the body and sits under the carpet instead of draining out.
issues.next: Have the leak traced and the drains cleared, then lift the carpet and padding to dry them. Water left under the carpet rots the floor and corrodes wiring and connectors under the seats.

issues.t: Underbody and front crossmember can rust through
issues.sym: Scaly, flaking metal under the floor and around the front crossmember and suspension mounts. Owners in salt states report sections rusted right through, sometimes with new clunks or a loose feel in the front end.
issues.why: Road salt attacks the thin underbody panels and the crossmember on these early RAV4s. Once the metal is pitted it keeps rotting from the inside, and the mounting points for suspension parts go with it.
issues.next: Have the underbody and every suspension mounting point checked on a lift before trusting the vehicle. Rust that has eaten through structure or a suspension mount is not safe to drive on and is often not worth repairing.
